summary: Successful remote PUTs execute pressure GC synchronously on async workers, delaying unrelated health work when available async capacity is exhausted.
scenario: Remote enabled and writable; real successful PUT to absent key; main store over its pressure trigger. One async worker is starved by one sweep. Additionally, with two async workers, 16 background upload tasks and a configured volume shard, two concurrent successful jobs can hold main and shard GC locks and wait for real SQLite writers, delaying health until those writers release.

evidence.point: Successful PUT publishes key presence, retires upload intent, calls maybe_evict_after_upload synchronously, then returns upload success.
Post-upload sweep stays inline; GC hint uses spawn_blocking for the same sweep.
Each shard has an independent gc.lock; another upload skips a held main lock and can enter a shard sweep.
Production replay and buffered uploads run through next_upload_job/run_upload_job in max(s3_concurrency,1) async tasks.
Executed two-worker/main+shard ordering regression FAIL; health latency 707.526 ms.
Same two-worker pipeline with one store PASS; health and all 31 peer uploads completed before writer release in this control execution.
18 samples: health blocked 3/3 with one async worker and 3/3 with two workers/two stores; progressed in every tested spare-capacity case.

trace: rustc wrapper publication -> durable upload spool/fire-and-forget -> server upload buffer or startup replay -> bounded channel -> next_upload_job -> run_upload_job -> do_upload -> successful PUT -> inline sweep(main, shards) -> real filesystem/SQLite operations and synchronous pacing sleep -> async health task waits for a worker

authority.source: production responsiveness failure mode; src/daemon.rs:8685-8689; Tokio 1.53.1 spawn_blocking documentation
authority.quote: Offload: a GC sweep is seconds of std::fs work ... never run it on an async worker (#281).

severity: Operational responsiveness and background upload-slot occupancy; conditional on remote writes, pressure and insufficient spare async capacity. Main+shard case is reachable on a two-worker runtime with 16 upload tasks. No data loss, corrupted cache, whole-Cargo slowdown, or normal idle 16-worker starvation was demonstrated. One shared store serializes full sweeps; configured shards permit concurrent sweeps. Three samples per capacity case; controlled SQLite contention is not an estimate of normal contention frequency.

summary: Multiple worktrees sharing one store do not by themselves create parallel full eviction sweeps.
checked: Read per-store gc.lock acquisition/release, main Store mutex lifetime, actual production upload worker scheduling; ran 32 durable-job samples with 2/16 async workers and 16 upload tasks.
closed_by: Tier 1: one-store/two-worker health progressed 3/3; 21-31 peer jobs completed before writer release. One-store/16-worker health progressed 3/3, all 31 peers finished early. Tier 2: src/daemon.rs:6769-6784 and store.rs:2584-2587 enforce a skip for another sweep of the same store.
reopens_if: Different real workloads show lost responsiveness with sufficient spare async workers, or non-GC synchronous operations occupy them; configured independent shards are separately admitted in D5.

summary: The constrained-runtime test does not establish ordinary sixteen-worker Cargo throughput slowdown.
checked: Replayed one-worker failure; tested 32-job one-store/two-store pipelines with 16 async and upload workers; inspected compiler client publication and daemon enqueue responses.
closed_by: Tier 1: 16-worker health progressed in all six samples; one store allowed 31/31 peer completion, two stores 30/31 while two slots were occupied. Tier 2: src/daemon.rs:4045-4047,7384-7437,8832-8855 distinguish enqueue/durable intent publication from background PUT/GC completion. No Cargo makespan was measured.
reopens_if: A controlled end-to-end realistic multi-worktree Cargo workload demonstrates a repeatable makespan or remote backlog cost caused by D5.

summary: D5 is not established as a cause of the current local-only setup described by prior evidence.
checked: Read remote-enable guard and do_upload no-remote/readonly/failed/already-present returns. Prior verification.md reports no remote configuration; this run did not inspect real user config.
closed_by: Tier 2: src/wrapper/remote.rs:8-30 and src/daemon.rs:4124-4154 prevent this successful-PUT trigger with no remote. Prior configuration observation is retained as prior evidence, not independently refreshed.
reopens_if: Current configuration enables remote writes and workloads generate actual successful PUTs under size pressure.

summary: Offloading D5 does not eliminate the separate durable-publication GC-lock wait.
checked: Traced wrapper.rs:4952 -> wrapper/remote.rs:27 -> send_upload_job -> persist_upload_job; read cross-process acquire_gc_lock and daemon async persistence helper.
closed_by: Tier 2: src/daemon.rs:724-778 and 8853 acquire GC lock before publication; moving the sweep to the blocking pool preserves that durability ordering.
reopens_if: A separately approved durability mechanism permits publication without waiting for GC while still protecting payload integrity.
